content: Sister chromatid cohesion protein DCC1 is a protein encoded by the DSCC1 gene in humans. To study the function of DSCC1, model organisms have been utilized. Specifically, a conditional knockout mouse line, named Dscc1tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi, was developed at the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute. This was part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program, a large-scale mutagenesis initiative aimed at creating and distributing animal models of human diseases for research purposes. Both male and female mice from this knockout line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening process to assess the consequences of DSCC1 gene deletion. A total of 24 tests were conducted on the mutant mice, and four significant abnormalities were identified. During gestation, very few homozygous mutant embryos were detected, and some of these embryos exhibited oedema. Consequently, the survival rate of homozygous mutants until the weaning stage was lower than expected. Among the homozygous mutants that survived, increased chromosomal instability was observed in a micronucleus test. Additionally, radiographic analysis revealed numerous skeletal abnormalities in these mice. Furthermore, DCC1 has been demonstrated to interact with the protein CHTF18.
